NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA exhibits exceptional fundamental health and trajectory: Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY, +20% QoQ) with EPS of $2.39 (+214.5% YoY), gross margins of 74.9%, operating cash flow of $50.3B, and a fortress balance sheet (debt-to-equity 0.043). The company dominates AI infrastructure with ~86% data center GPU market share, and Q2 guidance of ~$91B signals no deceleration. However, valuation is the key tension: at a P/E of 31.3x (as of 6/11), the stock is at the low end of its 30.6-66.8x 12-month range, having compressed significantly from 54-61x in early 2026 as earnings surged. This is cheap vs. its own recent history and reasonable for a company growing 85%+ with 75% gross margins. The near-term catalyst is the Q2 FY2027 earnings report (Aug 27) with 95% guided revenue growth, plus the $110B capital return plan (50%+ of FCF) announced at GTC Taipei. Risks include hyperscaler custom silicon competition, China export controls, and potential AI capex deceleration, but these are longer-term and well-flagged. The SpaceX IPO on June 12 and broader AI capex cycle ($700B projected for 2026) provide supportive context. Score reflects strong fundamentals and cheap vs. history valuation tempered by massive earnings beats,, but tempered by the fact that the stock has already run significantly and faces macro headwinds (inflation at 4.2%, rising rates, geopolitical tensions).
